name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+22 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely
Donavan McKinney enters the general with strong fundraising and outside support after defeating the incumbent in the primary
Republican nominee T. P. Nykoriak shows no reported fundraising or outside spending
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 98% to win
model.rationale: This Detroit-area seat's D+22 lean and the absence of any competitive general-election signals point to a comfortable Democratic hold. McKinney's fundraising edge and near-certain market pricing outweigh the modest uncertainty from an open seat with no polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Republican nominee within striking distance, or a surge of outside spending against McKinney, would be the first sign the open-seat dynamic is creating real risk.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Michigan's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Detroit-area seat, and incumbent Shri Thanedar is not on the ballot after losing his primary to Donavan McKinney. That primary result effectively settled the race's competitive phase; the general election now pits McKinney against Republican T. P. Nykoriak, along with several minor-party and independent candidates.

McKinney has raised about $1.4 million and benefits from outside spending in his favor, while the Republican campaign shows no reported fundraising or outside support. No public general-election polls are available, but prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 98% to win. The district's strong partisan lean makes a Democratic hold the clear expectation, with the main open-seat uncertainty reflected in a somewhat wider error range than a typical safe incumbent seat.
